title: 📚 School Survival Dashboard: Four-Course Check-In
desc: Check what's happening in each Grade 11 course. Use actual dates and marks if you know them; otherwise write 'not sure' and make a plan to check.
write: Which course needs your attention first, and why?
Use your upcoming deadlines, understanding and workload to decide.
What is one school success from this week?
It can be a completed task, a question you asked or a strong start.

title: 🎃 The Five-Minute Mystery
desc: Investigate what really happened when you tried starting homework before Roblox or YouTube.
pick: Over the last five school days, on how many days did you try the five-minute homework start?
write: Think back over the last five school days. What happened when you got home?
Describe when you started homework, when you used Roblox or YouTube, and what helped or got in the way.
Why is getting started easier at school than at home?
Think about your environment, routines and distractions.
Looking back at those five school days, what would you change next week?
Explain one practical adjustment.

title: 👻 Procrastination Detective
desc: Identify the thought, feeling and action behind avoidance.
pick: I don't know where to begin
What is a useful response to that thought?
Start gaming without a stopping point
write: Describe a recent time you delayed starting.
What were you thinking? What did you do instead?
Rewrite that thought as a helpful instruction to yourself.
Example: I only need to open the assignment and read the first question.

title: 🧟 Escape the Distraction Zone
desc: Put the after-school routine in an order you could realistically follow.

items: Arrive home and put away school things
Have a snack and take a planned short break
Open the chosen assignment and set up materials
Work on the first five-minute action
Decide whether to continue or schedule another block
Enjoy gaming or YouTube during planned free time

write: Why did you choose this order?
Explain how it balances rest, schoolwork and gaming.
What might interrupt this routine?
Give one realistic obstacle and a solution.

title: 🧪 The Assignment Breakdown Lab
desc: A major assignment feels overwhelming. Put the steps in a workable order, then apply the strategy to your own work.

items: Read the assignment instructions and rubric
Identify what must be submitted and when
List the smaller pieces of work
Review progress and plan the next block

write: Choose a real school assignment.
Include the subject and what you need to produce.
Write the first three small steps you will take.
Make each step specific enough to start without guessing.
What would count as a successful five-minute start?
Finishing the whole assignment is not required.

title: 🕸️ The Time-Estimation Lab
desc: Plan realistically rather than assuming everything will be quick.
pick: Three tasks take 10, 15 and 20 minutes. How long altogether?
You predicted 20 minutes but needed 35. What is the difference?
Allow time for steps and interruptions
write: Estimate how long a real assignment will take.
Break it into at least three steps with estimated minutes.
What could make it take longer?
Explain how you would adjust your plan.

title: 🔮 Priority Sorting: The Haunted Deadline Board
desc: Move each fictional task into the most useful priority group. Tap a category or drag the task to a box.

items: Optional club poster with no deadline
Review notes for a quiz in four days

write: Explain one of your priority decisions.
Why does that task belong in that group?
Which real assignment should you prioritize this week?
Explain your choice.

title: 🧙 Build Your Homework Escape Plan
desc: Create a routine that works for your actual school week.
pick: Where is your best homework starting spot?
What will you do when you miss your planned start?
write: What exact assignment will you start?
Course, task and first action.
When and where will you start?
Choose a realistic school day, time and place.
How will you keep Roblox or YouTube from interrupting?
Choose a strategy you are willing to use.
What is your backup plan if you get stuck?
Explain what you will do rather than abandoning the task.

title: 🕹️ After-School Decision Simulator
desc: Choose how to respond to a real-life distraction.
pick: Friends invite you to game before homework. What is your best move?
Plan a short break, then start five minutes
You are stuck on question one. What next?
Identify what is confusing and ask for help
write: Explain the consequences of your first choice.
Consider tonight and tomorrow.
Write an if-then plan for the next time gaming interrupts homework.
If ___, then I will ___.
What would make your plan realistic?
Think about your usual routine.

title: 🧠 Instruction Decoder
desc: Turn a complex assignment into clear steps.
write: Read this fictional assignment: Compare two energy sources in 400–500 words, use three credible sources, add a graph and submit a cited PDF by Friday. List every requirement.
Write a checklist.
Which requirement should you confirm first, and why?
Explain your decision.
Write a specific clarification question for the teacher.
Ask about something that affects your work.
How will you track your checklist?
Choose a practical system.

title: 🧩 Project Breakdown Challenge
desc: Break a large project into smaller actions.
write: Choose a real assignment and identify its final product.
What must be submitted?
List at least eight steps needed to complete it.
Number your steps.
Which steps depend on earlier steps?
Explain two dependencies.
Which two steps could you complete in a 25-minute work block?
Make a realistic estimate.
What is the first five-minute action?
Be precise.

title: ⏳ Time Budget Challenge
desc: Calculate time, then design a realistic schedule.
pick: You have 90 minutes. Three tasks take 25, 30 and 20 minutes. How much time is left?
A 10-minute break and 5-minute setup leave how much of 90 minutes?
write: Write a 90-minute schedule with actual start and end times.
Include setup, work, break and buffer.
What happens if your first task takes 15 extra minutes?
Explain how you would adjust.
How could you compare predicted and actual work times?
Design a simple tracking method.

title: 🦇 Distraction Defence Experiment
desc: Evaluate strategies instead of guessing what works.
pick: Which distraction is hardest to manage?
write: List three possible ways to reduce your main distraction.
Make them realistic.
Choose one strategy to test for three school days.
Describe the test.
How will you measure whether it helped?
What evidence will you collect?
What could cause the experiment to fail?
Create a backup plan.

title: 📨 Ask-for-Help Communication Quest
desc: Practise communicating clearly before a deadline.
pick: Which question would help a teacher respond?
I understand the outline, but how should I cite the graph?
write: Draft a respectful message about a confusing assignment.
Include what you tried, the problem and a question.
What useful work could you do while waiting for a reply?
Identify a different step.
What is one real question you might need to ask this week?
Name the course and question.

title: 🎯 Four-Course Action Board
desc: Turn your school check-in into a workable plan.
write: Physics: what is the next action, deadline and estimated duration?
Be specific.
English: what is the next action, deadline and estimated duration?
Be specific.
Communications Technology: what is the next action, deadline and estimated duration?
Be specific.
Chemistry: what is the next action, deadline and estimated duration?
Be specific.
Which two actions matter most? Explain why.
Compare deadlines and importance.
What will you start tomorrow before gaming?
Name the exact first action.

title: 🪞 Evidence-Based Reflection
desc: Use your own experiences to evaluate progress.
write: What evidence from the last five school days shows whether the five-minute rule helped?
Describe what actually happened.
Compare your ideal routine with your actual routine.
What causes the difference?
What strength helps you start tasks at school?
How could you use it at home?
Write a testable prediction for next week.
If I ___, then I expect ___ on ___ days.
What should Laura ask you about next session?
Make it specific.

title: 🏆 Unlock Next Week
desc: Reflect on what you learned and choose a manageable challenge.
pick: How confident are you about the five-minute rule?
How many school days will you practise?
write: What is the most useful strategy you learned today?
Explain why it might work for you.
Write your challenge for next week.
Include what you will start, when, and how you will measure success.
What should Laura ask you about next session?
Choose a question that would help you reflect honestly.

title: 🎃 BONUS: Halloween Trivia Vault
desc: Optional fun round if you have time. Choose an answer, see feedback and try to unlock the trivia trophy!
trivia: Which vegetable was traditionally carved into lanterns in parts of Ireland and Scotland before pumpkins became popular?
Turnips were used for early jack-o'-lanterns.
Nocturnal animals are active mostly at night.
Which planet has the shortest day?
If 12 houses each give 3 candies, how many candies is that?
Which animal uses echolocation to navigate in darkness?
Many bats use echoes to locate objects and prey.
write: Which trivia question surprised you?
Tell Laura something new you learned.
